mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best defines inflorescence?

options.A: Inflorescence is the arrangement of multiple flowers on a common floral axis.
options.B: Inflorescence is a single flower with modified petals.
options.C: Inflorescence is the pattern of leaf arrangement on a stem.
options.D: Inflorescence is the fruiting body formed after pollination.

mcqs.answer: Inflorescence is the arrangement of multiple flowers on a common floral axis.
mcqs.explanation: Inflorescence refers specifically to how many flowers are organized on a single floral axis. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated structures (a single flower, leaf phyllotaxy, and fruit, respectively).

mcqs.question: In a racemose inflorescence, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The main axis continues to grow and produces flowers laterally, with the youngest flowers at the apex.
options.B: The main axis terminates in a flower, and subsequent flowers arise from lateral buds.
options.C: All flowers are borne at the same level forming a flat cluster.
options.D: Flowers develop from the base upward, with the oldest at the tip.

mcqs.answer: The main axis continues to grow and produces flowers laterally, with the youngest flowers at the apex.
mcqs.explanation: Racemose (indeterminate) inflorescences keep the main stem growing; lateral flowers are produced and the youngest buds are at the top. Option B describes cymose (determinate) inflorescences, C describes a corymb, and D reverses the age gradient.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic distinguishes a cymose inflorescence from a racemose one?

options.A: The terminal flower blooms first, stopping the main axis growth.
options.B: The main axis keeps elongating and produces newer flowers at the tip.
options.C: Flowers are arranged in a spiral pattern along the axis.

mcqs.answer: The terminal flower blooms first, stopping the main axis growth.
mcqs.explanation: In cymose (determinate) inflorescences, the apex forms a flower first, halting further elongation of the main axis. Option B describes racemose growth, C is unrelated to inflorescence type, and D is not a defining feature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following plants exhibits a racemose inflorescence?

options.A: Lily (Lilium) – flowers arranged along an elongated axis
options.D: Orchid (Orchidaceae) – spike-like but not a typical raceme

mcqs.answer: Lily (Lilium) – flowers arranged along an elongated axis
mcqs.explanation: Lilies bear their flowers on an elongated, indeterminate axis, a classic raceme. Tomatoes have a determinate (cymose) inflorescence, sunflowers possess a capitulum, and orchids usually have a spike or raceme but the given description fits lily best.

mcqs.question: Inflorescence is best described as:

options.A: The arrangement of a group of flowers on a common axis, distinct from a single flower.
options.B: A single flower with multiple petals.
options.C: The leaf arrangement on a stem.
options.D: The fruiting structure that develops after fertilization.

mcqs.answer: The arrangement of a group of flowers on a common axis, distinct from a single flower.
mcqs.explanation: Inflorescence specifically refers to a cluster of flowers organized on a shared axis, differentiating it from an individual flower (option B). Options C and D describe unrelated plant parts.

mcqs.question: A plant has an elongated main axis that keeps growing, bearing flowers laterally, with the youngest buds at the tip. This pattern is an example of which inflorescence type?
mcqs.explanation: The description matches the indeterminate growth of a racemose inflorescence, where the axis continues to elongate and newer (younger) flowers are produced at the apex. Cymose (determinate) inflorescences stop growth after the terminal flower, while umbels and capitula have different architectures.

mcqs.question: Which of the following plants typically displays a cymose (determinate) inflorescence?
mcqs.explanation: Tomato plants produce a determinate, cymose inflorescence where the terminal flower blooms first, halting further elongation. Mugwort and Lily have racemose inflorescences, while wheat bears a spike.

mcqs.question: A gardener observes a plant whose flowers are arranged in a flat‑topped cluster where the outer flowers open first and the central flowers open later. Which type of inflorescence does this describe, and which common plant exemplifies it?
mcqs.explanation: A corymb has a flat‑topped appearance because lower pedicels are longer, causing outer (lower) flowers to open first. Yarrow is a classic example of a corymb. The other options describe different inflorescence types that do not match the described opening sequence.
